spatial_claims.claim: Circle with center F and diameter BC; BA drawn perpendicular to BC at endpoint B
D is a point on line BA that lies on or within the circle; FD joined
Triangle FBD has right angle at B (angle FBD = 90 degrees)
FD > FB by angle comparison in triangle FBD (angle FBD > angle BDF implies opposite side FD > FB)
D lies outside the circle since FD > radius FB
BG lies in the space between line BA and the circumference without cutting the circle
H is the foot of perpendicular from F to line BG; angle FHB is right
Angle FBG < angle FBA = 90 degrees; BG lies between BF and BA directions
In triangle FBH: angle FHB (90) > angle FBH (acute), so FB > FH
H lies inside the circle (FH < radius); BG passes from B on circle through interior point H
For any acute angle FBG, line BG falls between BA and diameter BC on the semicircle side
Any such line BG must cut the circumference (by Steps 9-13 argument)
The angle of the semicircle (between diameter and arc) contains every acute rectilineal angle at B
The horn angle (between tangent BA and arc) is less than any acute rectilineal angle

configuration_map: Configuration at point B: F is the center of the circle on line BC (the diameter). B is an endpoint of the diameter on the circumference. BA is perpendicular to BC at B (tangent line direction). The arc of the circle at B is tangent to BA and curves toward the diameter. Angular ordering at B from the diameter direction: BF (0 degrees), any line BG at acute angle, the arc tangent direction (= BA direction at 90 degrees), BA (90 degrees). For Part 1: Triangle FBD with F on diameter, B at the right-angle vertex, D on perpendicular line BA. For Part 2: Triangle FBH with F at center, H as perpendicular foot from F onto BG (right angle at H), B on circumference. For Part 3: Any ray from B between diameter and tangent enters the semicircle and must cross the arc again.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The right triangle arguments (Parts 1 and 2) correctly establish point positions relative to the circle. The angle comparisons (Part 3) follow logically from the interposition result. Minor expository issues (extraneous FA=FB in Step 3, imprecise containment language in Step 18) are notation weaknesses, not spatial configuration contradictions. No step requires a geometric configuration incompatible with another step.
